paper_metadata.title: Microstructures and mechanical properties of cast Nb–Ti–Si–Zr alloys

evidence.quote: The effect of Zr addition on the microstructures and mechanical properties of cast Nb–22Ti–16Si– xZr (x ¼ 0–4) alloys was investigated.
Nominal compositions of Nb–22Ti–16Si– xZr ( x ¼ 0–4) alloys (at.%): No. 1 62 22 16 0
The alloys used in this study were arc-melted by a non-consumable tungsten electrode under an argon atmosphere in a water cooled copper crucible.

XRD results reveal that the as-cast alloys consist of three phases, which are Nbss, (Nb) 3Si and g(Nb)5Si3.
in the as-cast condition the microstructures are composed of white large Nbss dendrites, gray (Nb) 3Si matrix, black g(Nb)5Si3 phases.
The g(Nb)5Si3 phase tends to exist at the interface between Nbss and (Nb) 3Si.

When Zr content is up to 2 at.%, a ﬁne scale eutectic structure of Nbss/ g(Nb)5Si3 forms at the interface between Nbss and (Nb) 3Si
As seen in Fig. 2 (c)–(e), the eutectic region in the microstructures increases from 10.79% to 37.89% with increasing Zr content.

The increase in yield stress at ambient temperature can mainly be attributed to solid solution strengthening and the formation of lamellar structure.
The lamellar eutectic structure has more interfaces to inhibit dislocation movement, which may cause the further increase of room temperature strength.
